name: Drawer
description: A modal panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen and can be dragged down to dismiss, for short tasks on phones. With snap points it also rests at several heights (a peek, half, nearly full) and is dragged between them. Open it with DialogTrigger.

title.description: Heading, also used as the drawer accessible name. Without a title, pass aria-label.

description.description: Short supporting text under the title.

portalContainer.description: Draw the panel and its backdrop inside this element instead of over the whole page. Use it to show a sheet inside a preview, a framed app or a phone mock. The element must be positioned (relative) and clip its overflow.

isDismissable.description: Closes on backdrop click and on a swipe or drag down. Esc always closes.

snapPoints.description: Heights the drawer can rest at, as shares of the available height (the screen, or the portalContainer): [0.4, 0.9] rests at 40% and 90%. They are kept between 0.1 and 1 and put in order. Drag the handle or header up and down to move between them; a drag down from the lowest closes it when isDismissable. Without snapPoints the drawer is as tall as its content, up to 90% of the screen.

snap.description: Which snap point is showing, as an index into the sorted snapPoints, to control it. Use with onSnapChange.

defaultSnap.description: Which snap point it opens at, as an index into the sorted snapPoints, when you do not control it.

onSnapChange.description: Called with the new index when the drawer settles on another snap point.

labels.description: The words for the keyboard button that changes the height, for translation: { expand, collapse, expanded, collapsed }. Only used with two or more snap points.

children.description: Body and actions. A function receives close().

keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the drawer
With snap points: Tab to the Expand or Collapse button (shown when it has focus), Enter or Space steps to the next height, Arrow Up and Arrow Down move up and down
requirements: Focus moves into the drawer on open and returns to the trigger on close
Content behind the drawer is hidden from assistive technology
Page scroll is locked while open
Dragging is an extra way to close: Esc and any close button in the content always work
The slide animation and the drag settle are turned off when the user prefers reduced motion
The drawer is at most 90% of the viewport height and its body scrolls
With snap points, dragging is never the only way to change the height: a button, shown when it has focus, does it with the keyboard and screen readers, and the new height is announced
With snap points the body scrolls inside the visible height, so every part of the content stays reachable
screenReader: Opening announces a dialog with the drawer title
The description is read after the title
The drag handle is hidden from assistive technology
Closing announces the button that opened it (focus is back there)
With snap points: "Expand, button", then "Expanded" in the status region after it is pressed

use_when: A short task or a few choices on a phone, within thumb reach
Actions for one item, such as share or move
Content that is useful at a glance and better with more room: a peek at a result list, details over a map, a player's queue
avoid_when: A side panel on large screens: use Sheet
A short confirmation: use Dialog or AlertDialog
anti_patterns: Making dragging the only way to close it: always offer an action button too
Long multi-step flows inside a drawer
More than three snap points: the heights become hard to tell apart
A lowest snap point so small that nothing useful shows
